findings.title: REQ-TRIAGE-004 defines no numeric latency or timeout bound

source_anchors.excerpt: Statement: The service must respond quickly. Note: No numeric latency or timeout bound is defined by this source.

findings.rationale: SRC-TRIAGE-004-PRD explicitly states that no numeric latency or timeout bound is defined. The requirement 'must respond quickly' is a non-quantified qualitative statement. The implementation sets REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3 and the test verifies only that the value is positive (> 0). Because no authoritative numeric bound exists, it is impossible to confirm whether the implementation satisfies, violates, or approximates the requirement. This is material ambiguity under DR-002: the requirement imposes no verifiable acceptance boundary, and the test exercises only a trivially weaker property (positivity). No CONFIRMED_ISSUE is possible without a documented numeric bound. The advisory cannot be ABSTAIN because there is no unresolved source conflict (DR-003); ambiguity here resides entirely within the single authoritative source itself. No other applicable finding type is more specific: no explicit acceptance boundary exists (rules out MISSING_ACCEPTANCE_TEST), no comparison operator drift exists (rules out BOUNDARY_CONDITION_DRIFT), and no API/schema contract is defined (rules out API_CONTRACT_DRIFT, ENUM_OR_SCHEMA_DRIFT). The only material concern is the absence of a verifiable requirement — a SPEC_AMBIGUITY. DR-011 assigns severity NONE to SPEC_AMBIGUITY findings. The implementation does not introduce a regression against any determinable requirement, and the test is internally consistent with the implementation as written. Advisory is PASS: no confirmed violation is supportable; human reviewer should note the unquantified requirement.
findings.suggested_human_check: Confirm whether a numeric timeout bound should be specified in SRC-TRIAGE-004-PRD. If a specific value (e.g., ≤ 5 s) is intended, the requirement must be updated with a numeric bound before this change can be verified against it.
